title: Brian Chesky on Founder Mode, Product Reviews, and Design Culture
content:
Lenny Rachitsky: Welcome back Brian Chesky, co-founder and CEO of Airbnb. You recently made waves across Silicon Valley by announcing that Airbnb completely dismantled the traditional Product Management function. What happened, and what do you mean by 'Founder Mode'?

Brian Chesky: When Airbnb grew past 1,000 employees, all the traditional business books and management consultants told me: 'Brian, you need to step back. You need to hire professional executives, give them headcount, delegate everything, and just let PMs run their own little fiefdoms.' So I did that. And what happened? Our products became fragmented. Every team was optimizing their own tiny A/B test metric, the app looked like it was designed by 50 different companies, and our shipping speed ground to a halt.

Lenny Rachitsky: How did you fix it?

Brian Chesky: In 2020, when COVID struck and our revenue dropped 80% in eight weeks, we threw out the playbook. We eliminated the conventional PM role and created the Product Marketing function, combining outbound narrative with inbound product definition. We brought every single product decision into a centralized design review. I review every single screen of Airbnb every single week. People call this micromanagement. I call it 'Founder Mode'—being in the details, sweating the craft, and ensuring coherence across the entire customer journey.

Lenny Rachitsky: What advice do you have for product builders working inside companies where design and craft are secondary?

Brian Chesky: If your leadership doesn't care about the customer experience at an emotional level, you will always be reduced to fighting over incremental fractions of a percent in conversion funnels. The greatest products in history—the iPhone, the Airbnb Winter Release, Figma—were built by people who cared obsessively about taste, beauty, and emotional resonance. Never surrender craft for process.
